questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves is a pure sensory nerve?
questions.explanation: The olfactory nerve is a pure sensory cranial nerve and carries no motor fibers. The source uses the mnemonic 'Some Say Money Matters But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter More' to classify cranial nerves as sensory, motor or mixed.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following brainstem nuclei is not derived from the alar plate?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nucleus is not derived from the alar plate; it is a motor nucleus derived from the basal plate. In the developing neural tube, the basal plate forms motor nuclei and the alar plate forms sensory nuclei. The rhombic lip gives rise to the cerebellum and its nuclei.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: The arrangement of the functional columns of cranial nerve nuclei from ventral to dorsal aspect in the brainstem is as follows:

options.text: Visceral Efferent > Somatic Efferent > Visceral Afferent > Somatic Afferent
Somatic Efferent > Visceral Efferent > Visceral Afferent > Somatic Afferent
Somatic Afferent > Visceral Afferent > Visceral Efferent > Somatic Efferent
Visceral Efferent > Visceral Afferent > Somatic Afferent > Somatic Efferent

questions.correctAnswerText: Somatic Efferent > Visceral Efferent > Visceral Afferent > Somatic Afferent
questions.explanation: From ventral to dorsal, the functional columns are Somatic Efferent > Visceral Efferent > Visceral Afferent > Somatic Afferent. Motor columns lie ventrally in the basal plate and sensory columns dorsally in the alar plate, with visceral columns nearer the sulcus limitans than somatic columns.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves does not contain neurons from the general somatic efferent column?
questions.explanation: The facial nerve does not contain neurons from the general somatic efferent (GSE) column. GSE is represented by nuclei of III, IV, VI and XII. Facial nerve motor fibers belong to the special visceral efferent column, while its parasympathetic component arises from the superior salivatory nucleus in the general visceral efferent column.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not included in the special visceral efferent column?
questions.explanation: The dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus is not part of the special visceral efferent (SVE) column. SVE supplies muscles derived from pharyngeal arches and includes the motor nucleus of V, motor nucleus of VII and nucleus ambiguus. The dorsal motor nucleus of X belongs to the general visceral efferent column.

The dorsal motor nucleus of X belongs to the general visceral efferent column.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nuclei do not belong to the general visceral efferent column?
questions.explanation: Nucleus ambiguus does not belong to the general visceral efferent (GVE) column; it is SVE. GVE contains parasympathetic nuclei: Edinger-Westphal (III), superior salivatory (VII), inferior salivatory (IX) and dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (X).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which cranial nerve nuclei are present in both the general somatic efferent and general visceral efferent columns?
questions.explanation: The oculomotor nerve has nuclei in both GSE and GVE columns: the oculomotor motor nucleus is GSE and the Edinger-Westphal nucleus is GVE.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The oculomotor nerve has nuclei in both GSE and GVE columns: the oculomotor motor nucleus is GSE and the Edinger-Westphal nucleus is GVE.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerve nuclei is not a part of the special visceral afferent (SVA) column?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nucleus is not part of the special visceral afferent column. It is a general somatic efferent motor nucleus supplying the superior oblique muscle. SVA components are associated with taste/visceral-special sensory pathways.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The trochlear nucleus is not part of the special visceral afferent column. It is a general somatic efferent motor nucleus supplying the superior oblique muscle. SVA components are associated with taste/visceral-special sensory pathways.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nerves is not involved in olfaction?
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal nerve is purely motor and is not involved in olfaction. The source notes contributions of trigeminal, glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves to olfactory-related sensation/modulation.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 72-year-old patient who suffered a stroke is unable to swallow food. On examination, the gag reflex is absent. The motor nucleus of the vagus nerve involved here emerges from ______ of the brainstem.
questions.explanation: Fibers from nucleus ambiguus emerge through the posterolateral sulcus of the brainstem. Nucleus ambiguus contains motor components associated with cranial nerves IX, X and XI. The source also summarizes vagal components: dorsal vagal nucleus for parasympathetic output, nucleus ambiguus for pharynx/larynx/palate, nucleus tractus solitarius for viscero-sensory input, and spinal trigeminal nucleus for somatic sensory input from outer ear/dura.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 69-year-old male presented with diplopia. Investigations revealed an aneurysm of the right anterior inferior cerebellar artery that is directly impinging on the nerve arising at the pontomedullary junction. Which of the following extraocular muscles is likely to be paralyzed?
questions.explanation: The lateral rectus is most likely paralyzed because it is supplied by cranial nerve VI, which emerges at the pontomedullary junction. CN VI, VII and VIII arise at this junction. Superior oblique is supplied by IV; most other extraocular muscles by III.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The lateral rectus is most likely paralyzed because it is supplied by cranial nerve VI, which emerges at the pontomedullary junction. CN VI, VII and VIII arise at this junction. Superior oblique is supplied by IV; most other extraocular muscles by III.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 34-year-old presents to the casualty with a history of blunt force trauma to the head. A small lesion was found on the dorsal aspect of the brainstem on imaging. Which of the following nerves could be injured at the site?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nerve is the only cranial nerve that exits the brainstem from its dorsal surface, so a dorsal brainstem lesion can injure it. The other listed cranial nerves exit ventrally.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The trochlear nerve is the only cranial nerve that exits the brainstem from its dorsal surface, so a dorsal brainstem lesion can injure it. The other listed cranial nerves exit ventrally.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following nerves exits anterior to the marked structure in the image?
questions.explanation: The marked structure is the olive. The hypoglossal nerve emerges anterior to the olive through the groove between the pyramid and olive (preolivary/anterolateral sulcus).
questions.structuredExplanationText: The marked structure is the olive. The hypoglossal nerve emerges anterior to the olive through the groove between the pyramid and olive (preolivary/anterolateral sulcus).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which is the thickest cranial nerve?
questions.explanation: The trigeminal nerve is the thickest cranial nerve. The trochlear nerve is the most slender cranial nerve.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The trigeminal nerve is the thickest cranial nerve. The trochlear nerve is the most slender cranial nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following cranial nerves does not carry parasympathetic fibers?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nerve does not carry parasympathetic fibers. Parasympathetic cranial outflow is carried with III, VII, IX and X.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The trochlear nerve does not carry parasympathetic fibers. Parasympathetic cranial outflow is carried with III, VII, IX and X.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following sensations is not perceived by the spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve?
questions.explanation: Proprioception is perceived by the mesencephalic nucleus of the trigeminal nerve, not the spinal trigeminal nucleus. The source contrasts the trigeminal nuclei: mesencephalic for proprioception, principal sensory for touch/pressure, spinal nucleus for pain and temperature (plus some touch), and motor nucleus for muscles of mastication and related first-arch muscles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A patient with trigeminal neuralgia presents with a flare-up of the condition. The nucleus receiving the sensory afferent extends from the chief sensory nucleus in the pons up to the:
questions.explanation: In trigeminal neuralgia, pain and temperature afferents relay in the spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve. This nucleus continues inferiorly from the chief sensory nucleus through the medulla to approximately the second cervical spinal segment.
questions.structuredExplanationText: In trigeminal neuralgia, pain and temperature afferents relay in the spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve. This nucleus continues inferiorly from the chief sensory nucleus through the medulla to approximately the second cervical spinal segment.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the nerve involved in the palsy shown below is false?

options.text: It divides into upper and lower divisions in its anterior part in the cavernous sinus.
Its divisions enter the orbit through the middle part of the superior orbital fissure.
It lies between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries in the interpeduncular fossa.
The nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion.
questions.explanation: The image shows oculomotor palsy. The false statement is that the nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion; these fibers travel with the nerve to inferior oblique. The oculomotor nerve passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, runs in the lateral wall of cavernous sinus, divides into superior and inferior divisions and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure/common tendinous ring.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The image shows oculomotor palsy. The false statement is that the nerve to inferior rectus carries parasympathetic fibers to the ciliary ganglion; these fibers travel with the nerve to inferior oblique. The oculomotor nerve passes between the posterior cerebral and superior cerebellar arteries, runs in the lateral wall of cavernous sinus, divides into superior and inferior divisions and enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure/common tendinous ring.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: A 36-year-old male was brought to the emergency department after suffering a head injury in a road traffic accident. CT revealed a skull base fracture. The fracture line extended along the apex of the petrous bone involving Dorello's canal. Which of the following cranial nerves is susceptible to injury?
questions.explanation: The abducens nerve traverses Dorello's canal and is therefore susceptible to injury in a fracture involving the petrous apex. Dorello's canal lies at the petrous apex beneath the petrosphenoidal (Gruber) ligament.
questions.structuredExplanationText: The abducens nerve traverses Dorello's canal and is therefore susceptible to injury in a fracture involving the petrous apex. Dorello's canal lies at the petrous apex beneath the petrosphenoidal (Gruber) ligament.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: Which of the following is not used for the identification of the facial nerve trunk?
questions.explanation: The inferior belly of omohyoid is not used to identify the facial nerve trunk. The source describes anterograde landmarks including the tragal pointer, posterior belly of digastric, squamotympanic fissure, styloid process and mastoid process, and a retrograde method tracing distal facial branches proximally.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.question: All of the following nerves are involved in the movement of the eyeball except:
questions.explanation: Structure A is the optic nerve (CN II), which is not involved in eyeball movement. The image labels optic (II), oculomotor (III), abducens (VI) and trochlear (IV) nerves. Extraocular movement is supplied by III, IV and VI: lateral rectus by VI, superior oblique by IV, and the remaining listed extraocular muscles by III.
